newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Dollar/mark gains seen fleeting.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Dollar/mark gains seen fleeting.

text.p: The dollar may gradually lose ground to the mark over the next two years if the U.S. economy falters while a rebound in Germany spurs higher interest rates, according to a Reuter quarterly U.S. economic poll.

"I think once we get into '97 and then into '98 we'll see the U.S. economy slow a little bit and maybe finally we'll see some of the European economies other than the (U.K.) pick up," said David Blitzer, chief economist and vice president at Standard and Poor's Corp.
That may boost German rates and attract more capital to Germany which will tend to push the mark slightly higher against the dollar.
The Bundesbank slashed its discount rate to 2.5 percent this year to help stimulate economic growth, while U.S. monetary policy largely steered a steady course.

The Reuters poll of 22 analysts showed, on average, the dollar at 1.5320 marks in the current quarter, 1.5398 in the second period of 1997, 1.4838 in the first quarter of 1998 and 1.5147 in the third period.
Individual forecasts varied widely; between fourth-quarter 1997 and third-quarter 1998, two analysts expect the dollar to peak at 1.70 marks and one predicts a plunge to 1.30.
Conference Board Chief Economist Gail Fosler said both U.S. and German interest rates will probably rise going forward.
However, higher U.S. inflation and an expanding trade deficit will likely pressure the dollar, said Fosler, a vice president of the business-supported research group.
The U.S. currency touched 1.5439 marks on Thursday morning.
